launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Dragon CRS-2 SpX-35
launches.missionDesc:
35th commercial resupply services mission to the International Space Station operated by SpaceX. The flight will be conducted under the second Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

flights.name: Starship SN8 | 12.5 km Flight
flights.missionDesc: The SN8 Starship prototype was destroyed when attempting to land after a first flight to an altitude of 12.5 km or 41,000 ft.
flights.failreason: Test completed set out objectives, but the vehicle failed to land successfully due to low pressure in the propellant header tanks cutting out the engines.
flights.label: SN8

flights.name: Starship SN9 | 10 km Flight
flights.missionDesc: The SN9 Starship performed a first flight similar to the one of SN8. It launched up to an altitude of 10 km or 33,000 ft, did a belly flop maneuver and a controlled descent to the landing pad where the landing flip maneuver was unsuccessful and resulted in the destruction of the prototype on impact.
flights.label: SN9

flights.name: Starship SN10 | 10 km Flight
flights.missionDesc: The SN10 Starship performed a test flight similar to SN8 and SN9. It launched up to an altitude of 10 km or 33,000 ft, did a belly flop maneuver followed by a controlled descent to the landing pad. Despite successfully performing the landing flip maneuver with its three Raptor engines, its vertical velocity was too high on landing, damaging its structure and resulting in an explosive destruction a
flights.label: SN10

flights.name: Starship SN11 | 10 km Flight
flights.missionDesc: The SN11 Starship prototype performed a test flight similar to SN8, SN9 and SN10. It launched up to an altitude of 10 km or 33,000 ft and did a belly flop maneuver followed by a controlled descent, but got destroyed during the landing maneuver.
flights.label: SN11

flights.name: Starship SN15 | 10 km Flight
flights.missionDesc: The SN15 Starship prototype will perform a test flight similar to SN8 to SN11. It will launch up to an altitude of 10 km or 33,000 ft and do a belly flop maneuver followed by a controlled descent to the landing pad.
flights.label: SN15

updates.text: The FAA has granted SpaceX a launch license for the 4th flight of Starship.
Starship flight 4 NET June 1, pending launch license
SpaceX has received the FAA license to launch Starship on its second test flight. Setting GO for the attempt on November 17 between 13:00 and 15:00 UTC (7-9am local).
SpaceX is targeting NET Mid-November for the second flight of Starship. This is subject to regulatory approval, which is currently pending.

journal.title: SDA T1TL-A
journal.text: No change. The launch is still NET Thu Oct 8, 3:54am ET (12:54am PT) from SLC-4E. The backup window is Fri Oct 9, 3:47am ET. It's B1103's 6th flight, and the booster lands at LZ-4. Launch Library shows it "Go."

journal.title: Other launches Oct 7
journal.text: None found. The next listed launch is a Starlink mission from Vandenberg on Sat Oct 10, 7–11pm ET.

journal.title: Crew-12 (Wed 8:05am ET)
journal.text: Undocked on time from Harmony with Meir, Hathaway, Adenot (ESA) and Fedyaev aboard. Splashdown is still targeted for Thu Oct 8 ~11:34am ET off California, with NASA coverage starting 10:20am ET.

journal.title: Starship Flight 15
journal.text: Quiet. There's still no official date; the unofficial NET of Oct 19 comes from air-traffic planning.

journal.text: (from $171.92), ending a 3-day win streak. Intraday range was $165.65–$171.31. Two things weighed on it. First, Reuters/FT reported SpaceX is seeking about $40B in debt to buy Nvidia AI chips: roughly $10B in bank loans plus $30B in investment-grade debt led b…

journal.title: Starmind
journal.text: No new facts. Al Jazeera ran a video explainer on the same "up to 1M AI sats" visualization, and the FCC is still reviewing the application. The $40B chip-debt report above is the real orbital/AI compute news today.

journal.title: SpaceXSI rename

journal.title: SDA T1TL-A did not launch Tuesday. SpaceX skipped the Oct 6 attempt and is now targeting Thu Oct 8 at 3:54 a.m. ET (12:54 a.m. PT) from Vandenberg SLC-4E.
journal.text: The backup is Fri Oct 9 at 3:47 a.m. ET. Late Monday evening (about 8:48 p.m. ET) SpaceX said it was passing on the Oct 6 window. It gave no reason for that or for Monday's last-minute auto-abort. Nothing launched and nothing landed. The booster is still B1103…

journal.title: Terafab/TSMC follow-up (CNBC, Tue)
journal.text: Intel fell about 3% for a second straight day on the prospect of a TSMC deal. TSMC was slightly lower Tuesday. BofA's Haas Liu expects component purchases rather than a TSMC license or co-run fab. There's still no deal. CNBC

journal.title: Crew-12 heads home
journal.text: NASA now has undocking NET Wed Oct 7 and splashdown off California Thu Oct 8 at about 11:34 a.m. ET, weather permitting. The crew is Meir, Hathaway, Adenot and Fedyaev. NASA

journal.title: Starship Flight 15
journal.text: There's still no official date. The unofficial NET Oct 19 still stands. An Oct 6 elonbuzz piece speculates that more Ship 42 testing could push it past October. That's speculation, not a SpaceX statement. Spike Today elonbuzz (speculative)

journal.title: Other launches
journal.text: I couldn't confirm any SpaceX launch on Oct 6. One "Starlink 10-33 on Oct 6" result turned out to be a March article. The next launches are T1TL-A (Oct 8) and Starlink 15-25 (Oct 10, 7 p.m. ET). Spaceflight Now schedule

journal.title: New: Starlink Community Host Beta waitlist.
journal.text: One kit serves several nearby users, who buy hourly, daily, weekly or monthly passes. The monthly pass covers up to 4 devices. Hosts provide the site, power and upkeep, and Starlink handles payments and access. There are no prices, revenue split or launch date…

journal.title: SDA T1TL-A scrubbed at the last second; no launch, no landing.
journal.text: Falcon 9 had an automatic abort in the final minute, just before T-0, around 4:28 a.m. ET. SpaceX said the "Vehicle and payload are in good health." The new target is NET Tue Oct 6 at 4:17 a.m. ET from Vandenberg SLC-4E, in a window of about 3:59–4:21 a.m. ET.…
